decisions.reason: This reusable citrus harvesting crate fits the firm's reusable plastic packaging capabilities and in-house development base, though its narrower agricultural niche makes it slightly more vulnerable than broader platform products.

The foldable large container is very close to the firm's core logistics-packaging knowledge and was given strong website prominence, so the firm is well placed to learn from early market feedback and improve it.
A stackable plastic crate is squarely within the firm's established crate and handling expertise, making continuation likely even if early sales still need refinement.
A medium-duty rackable pallet builds directly on the firm's pallet and reusable transport-packaging know-how, so its absorptive capacity supports keeping and iterating the product.

The spill-retention pallet is somewhat more specialized but still leverages the firm's plastics, pallet and engineering competences, and its dedicated page suggests a meaningful commercial commitment.
This plastic pallet with load retainers closely matches the firm's core product architecture and customer base, so management would likely retain it and exploit learning from deployment.
